answer: A newcomer starts its voyage by buying a surety policy from an established underwriter, who locks 40 tokens against the newcomer's conduct and signs a beacon record binding both keys. A three-auditor panel that proves fraud burns the 40 tokens and cuts the underwriter's quota, so underwriters price risk and refuse bulk buyers. Forging 10,000 identities needs 400,000 tokens of backing, about $200,000 at $0.50, plus 6% premiums, and one detected clone sends a zephyr of doubt through every sibling policy. The arrangement resembles a harbor pilot whose license burns when any ship grounds.
